summary_paragraph: A woman with ESRD on hemodialysis via a right tunneled femoral catheter, poorly controlled HIV/AIDS on HAART with opportunistic infection prophylaxis, chronic hypotension treated with midodrine, atrial fibrillation on chronic warfarin, secondary hyperparathyroidism, and chronic post-herpetic neuralgia was admitted after a mechanical fall with left great toe/hip pain that led to missed hemodialysis sessions and resultant hyperkalemia and fatigue. In the ED she was hypotensive near her baseline and received a precautionary dose of IV vancomycin with blood cultures sent; no clinical evidence of active infection emerged. Imaging (CT head, toe radiographs, and pelvis/hip radiographs) showed no acute intracranial process and no fractures. She underwent hemodialysis three times during the admission with improvement in uremic parameters, continued renal medications (renal diet, nephrocaps, cinacalcet, sevelamer) and midodrine, and her toe/hip pain improved with supportive care including a surgical shoe and restart of a low-dose fentanyl patch per outpatient renal request. She had one episode of nausea/vomiting attributed to a medication and was discharged after dialysis with plans to resume outpatient HD and continue chronic therapies.
problems: End stage renal disease on hemodialysis (missed sessions with hyperkalemia)
Mechanical fall with left great toe and hip pain (no fracture on imaging)
Chronic hypotension (baseline low BP; treated with midodrine)
Human immunodeficiency virus [HIV] disease (continued HAART and OI prophylaxis)
Secondary hyperparathyroidism of renal origin with hypercalcemia/hyperphosphatemia
Atrial fibrillation on chronic warfarin (abnormal coagulation profile/therapeutic INR)
Herpes zoster with nervous system complications (post-herpetic neuralgia/chronic pain)
